The world keeps you waiting. Here is a way to understand what it is doing.
A queue looks like people standing still. Underneath it, work is arriving, capacity is being shared,
A long shared line can move better than several short ones. The useful question is who gets the next
A small delay can recruit the whole route to make itself bigger. The clue is in the gap ahead.
The case for an empty minute
A service can have enough capacity on average and still make people wait. Spare time is part of how
Two routes can both average a bus every ten minutes. You can still wait much longer for one of them.

text.text: About the way daily life works.
The world keeps you waiting. Here is a way to understand what it is doing.
A queue looks like people standing still. Underneath it, work is arriving, capacity is being shared,
A long shared line can move better than several short ones. The useful question is who gets the next
A small delay can recruit the whole route to make itself bigger. The clue is in the gap ahead.
The case for an empty minute
A service can have enough capacity on average and still make people wait. Spare time is part of how
Two routes can both average a bus every ten minutes. You can still wait much longer for one of them.
Count the people, find the wait
Little’s law links the crowd in a system to the rate people pass through it. First, decide where the
A clock is only half the wait
Uncertainty, explanation and the rules of the line belong in the design of a wait. They do not repla
